name: cohere_forward_deployed_engineer_agentic_platform_uk_public_sector
role: Forward Deployed Engineer, Agentic Platform (UK Public Sector)
gaps_acknowledged: No production multi-step agent shipped using ReAct or Plan-and-Execute patterns (stated plainly in the cover letter)
No active DV security clearance, which the posting says is highly preferred
No named experience with vector databases or agent orchestration frameworks
Production software engineering at scale (observable, scalable services) is not yet proven; profile records this as a growth area
sponsorship_note: not stated - the posting says nothing about visa sponsorship either way. Candidate currently has the right to work in the UK without sponsorship and would need Skilled Worker sponsorship later; this is stated in the cover letter.
key_tailoring_decisions: Led the DS Digital Technology entry with the BeiGene medical-AI work reframed as forward-deployed delivery into a regulated customer: a 246-question benchmark and safety rubric with red-line rules adopted as the client's acceptance standard, a Python pipeline over six LLM APIs with retrieval and search augmentation scoring 2,400+ responses, and a medically reviewed knowledge graph tested with blinded paired A/B tests. This maps directly onto the posting's demand for RAG plus evaluation frameworks measuring agent accuracy and safety.

Rewrote the CV skills block around the posting's own headings (LLM Stack, Evaluation Frameworks) and used the UK Biobank dissertation as the credential for large, sensitive, controlled-access data, which is the public-sector angle.

Anchored the 'why Cohere' paragraph only on facts independently verified from cohere.com and cohere.com/north (North as an agentic platform deployed on-prem or in an isolated VPC, grounded in customer data), and declined to claim agent-building experience she does not have, gapping ReAct/Plan-and-Execute and DV clearance openly instead.
warnings: CLEARANCE: the posting states 'Active DV clearance is highly preferred'. It is preferred, not required, and it is not framed as a nationality gate, so this does not trip the profile's 'security clearance gated on citizenship' deal-breaker outright. However, Developed Vetting in the UK does in practice carry nationality and residency requirements, so a UK public-sector delivery role may become gated in later stages. The cover letter states plainly that she does not hold DV clearance. User should decide whether to submit.
SPONSORSHIP: the posting is silent on visa sponsorship. Cohere's own careers material was not confirmed to address sponsorship for this role, so this remains unverified rather than a stated positive.

TRAVEL: the posting requires 20-40% travel to work on-site with customers and partners. Per the evaluation framework, frequent travel is a FLAG to discuss, not a fail. The letter says she is comfortable with it.

PROCESS DEVIATION: the mandatory reviewer subagent could NOT be run. Three attempts were refused with 'Concurrent subagent limit reached' (20 sibling application agents running), and the tool instructed not to retry. I ran the Factual Grounding Audit, the AI-tells audit, the requirement-coverage check and the company research myself instead, and verified all Cohere claims directly against cohere.com and cohere.com/north. Self-audit caught and fixed four grounding drifts: 'Worked inside UK Biobank governance controls' (implied she navigated the access-approval process) softened to 'a controlled-access dataset'; 'ran blinded paired A/B tests' corrected to 'designed', matching the profile; 'Lead working sessions' softened to 'Present findings and recommendations'; and 'latency measurement' removed from the skills line as unevidenced, despite the posting naming latency. A second-opinion review is the one step the user may wish to repeat.
